glosses: To pass lightly; to glide along in an even, smooth course; to glide along near the surface.

examples.text: Not so when swift Camilla scours the plain, / Flies o'er the unbending corn, and skims along the main.

glosses: To pass near the surface of; to brush the surface of; to glide swiftly along the surface of.

examples.text: Homer describes Mercury as flinging himself from the top of Olympus, and skimming the surface of the ocean.

glosses: To hasten along with superficial attention.

examples.text: They skim over a science in a very night superficial survey.

glosses: To put on a finishing coat of plaster.

examples.text: Ceilings are lined with fibrous asbestos, the internal plastering being reduced to skimming alone.

glosses: To throw an object so it bounces on water.

examples.text: skimming stones

glosses: To ricochet.
To read quickly or describe summarily, skipping some detail.

examples.text: (through)
I skimmed the newspaper over breakfast.

glosses: To scrape off; to remove (something) from a surface
To clear (a liquid) from scum or substance floating or lying on it, by means of a utensil that passes just beneath the surface.

examples.text: to skim milk
to skim broth

glosses: To clear a liquid from (scum or substance floating or lying on it), especially the cream that floats on top of fresh milk.

examples.text: to skim cream

glosses: To steal money from a business before the transaction has been recorded, thus avoiding detection.

examples.text: Obviously, the longer cash sits around before being recorded, the more likely it is that a skimming fraud will occur.
[…] take this money without entering anything into the record-keeping system, thereby accomplishing a theft by skimming.

glosses: To surreptitiously scan a payment card in order to obtain its information for fraudulent purposes.
To become coated over.
Having lowered fat content.
A cursory reading, skipping the details.

examples.text: For a first quick appreciation of the approach, we recommend a fast reading of Chapter 1, then a skim through the figures of the next two chapters — glancing at the definitions of key concepts that appear below the figures in Chapters 2 and 3.

glosses: Skim milk.

examples.text: Two percent milk has only a fraction less fat than whole milk, so unless you are feeding a child or someone whose diet requires whole milk, skim is best.

glosses: The act of skimming.

examples.text: Then you could jump 150 years and enjoy a skim across the Solent in Britain's remarkable Hovercraft.

glosses: That which is skimmed off.
Theft of money from a business before the transaction has been recorded, thus avoiding detection.

examples.text: It's a hustle, but it keeps me busy. I can take in three to three-fifty a week, more with skims.

glosses: Dégarnir une chose de ce qu’elle a de meilleur.

examples.text: Il a écrémé cette bibliothèque, cette collection, ce cabinet de médailles.
Écrémer une affaire.

glosses: Ôter les scories du verre fondu ou des matières en fusion.
Définition manquante ou à compléter. (Ajouter) Laver, nettoyer.

examples.text: Des larmes écrémèrent ses gros yeux profonds.
